newsitem.title: UK: Sweden's Folksam announces record 1996 results.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Folksam announces record 1996 results.

text.p: Stockholm based insurer Folksam on Friday reported record 1996 profits of 6.882 billion crowns, an increase of 69 percent on 1995, and premiums of 11.867 billion.
The record result followed a drop in claims and a rise on investment income, Folksam said in a statement issued in London. Total assets rose 15 percent to 62.1 billion crowns.
The group said it increased its share of all the main sectors of the Swedish market including motor, household and life insurance.
Staff levels were reduced by 153 as part of a cost cutting programme based on heavy investment in information technology.
Folksam International, which has operations in London, Stockholm and Singapore, made a profit of 161 million crowns.
The conversion last November of the London market operation to branch status had resulted in more good quality business, Folksam International president Anders Henrikson said.

Folksam's London operation expects to write around 25 million stg of income this year, a similar amount to 1996, Colin Barber, chief executive officer of the London Branch of Folksam International Insurance Co Ltd, told Reuters.
London business, which is primarily reinsurance, is divided roughly equally between marine, non-marine and aviation, he added.
